comments.author: @wwalker6408
comments.text:
This is a great reality check on “AI running a business.” The experiments show real progress, but also why agents still stumble without guardrails. The biggest takeaway for me is the **scaffolding problem**—when you give AI clear procedures, tools, and constraints, performance jumps fast. Without them, it falls back into polite, unprofitable assistant mode.

AI agents don’t fail because they’re dumb—they fail because they’re under-structured.

Project Vend and Andon FM feel like early glimpses of something real: scalable, semi-autonomous businesses where humans design the systems and AI runs the day-to-day. Not ready to replace people yet—but definitely ready to change how businesses are built.

comments.text:
The thing everyone forgets is corporate inertia. C-suite executives are notoriously slow to adopt new technology. They don't want to do anything that messes with their proven formula for making money. They only adopt new technology years or even decades later after it's been fully proven out by many other smaller companies.
We'll definitely see the same thing with AI. We already are. Today, AI can already replace a huge number of jobs, but it isn't. Telemarketers, technical support specialists, secretaries, bank tellers, etc. the list goes on and on of what AI could already replace today, but hasn't. Why? Not because it can't, not because companies are blissfully unaware, but because the C-suite execs are overly cautious about messing with their formula.
If we had AGI tomorrow, I doubt we'd see a significant shift in how the world works for at least 5-10yrs. Many companies are only now adopting technology that was invented back in 2008.
